chapters.title: The Dinosaur on the Trail
chapters.text:
Dean is a small dinosaur. He likes to eat green leaves by the stream.

One day, Dean sees a trail in the mud. The trail is deep and wide.

"Wait!" says Dean. "Who made this trail?"

Dean goes down the trail. He sees a green fern. He sees a goat on a boat. But no big dinosaur.

Rain falls. Dean gets wet. He hides in an oak tree and eats a leaf.

Then the ground shakes. Boom! Boom! A huge dinosaur walks by. Her neck is long. Her feet are the size of Dean!

"Do not be afraid," she says. "I eat leaves too."

Dean grins. "Can we eat as a team?"

"Yes!" she says.

They eat green leaves all day by the stream. Dean is glad he read the trail.

Real kids can read about dinosaurs too. Facts and games wait for you!

chapters.title: Rain Day for the Green Dinosaur
chapters.text:
A big green dinosaur sat by the oak tree. She had to wait. The rain fell on her back.

"I need to eat," she said. "I will eat leaves."

She ate green leaves. Each leaf was wet with rain. Each leaf was sweet.

A goat came down the trail. The goat did not eat leaves. The goat ate oats.

"Wait for me!" said the goat. "Let us be a team."

So the dinosaur and the goat went up the trail. The rain fell. The leaves fell.

They ate on the trail. They ate in the rain. The goat ate oats. The dinosaur ate leaves.

Soon the rain went away. The sun came out. The trail was clean.

"That was a good meal," said the goat.

Maya can read about real dinosaurs, too. Kids can see dino facts and games and art. Real teams dig up dino bones each day!

transcript.title: The Dino Egg in the Oak Tree
transcript.text:
Maya finds a big egg near an oak tree. It is by the train track.

"Is it real?" she says. The egg has a crack.

Out pops a tiny dino! It has green skin and a long tail.

"I will call you Oat," Maya says.

Oat eats leaves from the oak tree. He eats beans. He eats a peach!

Maya reads a book to Oat. Facts about dinosaurs fill each page.

"Long ago, some dinos ate meat. Some ate seeds and leaves like you," she reads.

Oat needs a home. Maya makes a nest of hay near the road.

Rain falls. Oat sleeps in his nest. Maya keeps him dry with a coat.

In the morning, Oat is bigger! His feet are huge.

Maya gives a big squeal. "Soon you will not fit in this nest!"

Oat licks her cheek.
transcript.cover_scene: A girl kneeling beside a cracked speckled egg under a big oak tree as a tiny green baby dinosaur peeks out.

chapters.title: The Oak Tree Snack Team
chapters.text:
Rex is a small dinosaur. He sits by a big oak tree. He waits for his team.

"Wait for me!" calls Goat. Goat is not a dinosaur, but Goat is on the team.

Rex and Goat want to eat. They eat oats. They eat each leaf on the low branch. Each leaf is green and sweet.

Then rain! Rain taps the oak. Rain taps the oats. The team runs under the big oak tree.

"Wait," says Rex. "We can eat here!"

Goat eats oats. Rex eats a leaf. Each one gets a snack in the rain.

The rain stops. The oak drips. The team naps by the oak.

Scientists read about dinosaurs and find new facts each year. They tell us what dinosaurs ate: leaves, seeds, and more. Rex would say, "Eat each leaf! Wait for your team!"

Rain, oak, oats, leaf, team. Rex likes them all.

transcript.title: Oat and the Boat Race
transcript.text:
Oat the dino is big now. He can pull a boat!

Maya paints the boat green. She paints a tail on each side.

"Ready to race?" she calls.

Oat nods. He steps in the lake. The road of waves goes far.

Maya reads the rules out loud. "Stay in your lane. Wait for the beep."

Beep! The boats go. Oat kicks his feet. Spray soaks Maya's coat.

A red boat takes the lead. Maya feels sad.

Then a gust of wind fills the sail. Oat leaps! The green boat speeds up.

They reach the last float. Oat gives one big kick.

The green boat wins by a nose!

The team cheers. Maya gets a gold seal on a sheet of paper.

She reads it to Oat. "First place!"

Oat eats a peach to feast. Maya eats one too.
transcript.cover_scene: A large friendly green dinosaur pulling a small painted boat with a girl aboard across a sparkling lake, other boats behind.

chapters.title: Sea Beach Dino Feast
chapters.text:
Dean is a big dino. Dean likes the sea.

Each day, Dean eats by the sea. He eats a leaf. He eats a heap of leaves!

"Eat with me!" Dean peeps.

A small dino runs to the beach. Her name is Bea. Bea can eat, eat, eat!

Dean and Bea are a team. The team leaps in the sea. The team naps in the heat.

Bea finds a green leaf. Dean finds a leaf. Each leaf is a treat!

"Eat up, team!" says Bea.

The sea is neat and clean. The dino team eats a big meal.

Real dinos are fun to read about. Kids can read dino facts and see dino art. Dinos ate leaves long, long ago!

Dean and Bea nap in the heat. Each dino has sweet dreams of leaves by the sea.

transcript.title: Oat Paints the Dino Road
transcript.text:
Maya has a plan. She will make a dino road!

She gets paint. Red paint. Gray paint. A pail of white paint too.

Oat helps. He dips his tail in the pail. Then he paints the road!

The road goes past the oak tree. It goes past the lake. It goes past the goat pen.

Maya nails a sign by the road. She reads it out loud. "Dino Road. Stay in your lane!"

Soon a toad hops on the road. A snail creeps on the road. The goat walks on the road.

"Wait!" Maya calls. "This road is for dinos!"

Oat gives a big roar. But then he smiles.

"You may all come," Maya says. "Dinos like to share."

So the toad and the snail and the goat ride on Oat's back, down the long gray road.

chapters.title: Dino Reads the Big Leaf Map
chapters.text:
Rex is a big green dino. Rex can read.

Today Rex will read a map. The map is on a leaf. A big flat leaf!

"Team! Come here!" Rex calls.

The team runs up. Stomp, stomp, stomp.

Rex reads the leaf map. "We will eat at the top of the hill."

The team likes to eat. Rex likes to eat. It is meal time!

Up they go. Rex holds the leaf map. The team reads it too.

At the top, they see a heap of green plants. What a meal!

Rex takes a leaf. Munch! The team takes a leaf. Munch, munch!

"This is the best meal," says Rex.

Then Rex reads one last bit of the leaf map. "Real dino facts are in books," he reads. "Kids can read them and see dino art!"

The team can eat. The team can read. Go, team!

transcript.title: Oat and the Deep Cave
transcript.text:
Maya reads a new dino fact. "Some bones hide in deep caves!"

"Let's go, Oat," she says.

They take the gray road. They pass the oak tree. They reach a deep cave by the sea.

Inside it is dim. Maya holds a light. Oat keeps close.

Drip. Drip. Water leaks from the peak of the cave.

Then Maya sees it. A huge bone in the clay!

"Wait," she says. "Is this real?"

She brushes the clay away. The bone is long and pale.

Oat sniffs it. He gives a soft moan.

"Do not be sad," Maya says. "This dino lived long ago. Now she can teach us."

They place the bone in a crate. They haul it up the trail.

At home, Maya makes a neat sign: MAYA'S BONE.

Oat beams. What a team!

chapters.title: Two Letters, One Sound: Dino's ea Rule
chapters.text:
Here is a rule. When e and a sit side by side, they make one sound. They say "ee." Just one sound. Not two.

Meet Pia. Pia is a dino. Pia can read.

Pia sees a leaf. Say it: l - ea - f. Leaf. One sound in the middle.

Pia can eat. Say it: ea - t. Eat. One sound.

Pia is on a team. Say it: t - ea - m. Team. One sound.

Now look at two words. Pat. Pan. Those have a short a. But heap has ea. Heap says "ee."

Sam the dino can not read yet. Sam says "e-a" as two sounds. Pia taps the word. "One sound, Sam!"

Sam tries. "Leaf. Eat. Team." Sam did it!

The team sits on the beach. They read dino facts and eat a big meal.

transcript.title: The Dino Fair on Main Street
transcript.text:
A dino fair comes to Main Street! Maya and Oat go at dawn.

Booths fill the street. One booth has dino art. One booth has games. One booth sells sweet treats.

Maya reads a fact card out loud. "New dino facts are found each year!"

At the first booth, Maya paints a dino. She paints it teal with a gold tail.

At the next booth, she throws a ball at a stack of cans. She beats the game! She wins a toy dino.

Oat waits by the treat cart. He wants a snack.

Maya buys him oats and a peach. Oat eats it all in one gulp!

Then a man calls, "Who can roar the best?"

Oat takes a deep breath. ROAR!

The whole street claps. Oat wins a big blue sash.

What a neat day!

chapters.title: Dino Says It Slow
chapters.text:
Dino digs in the mud. He finds a big green l-ea-f. Say it slow: leef. Leaf!

Dino is not fast. Dino says it slow. That is a good trick.

Now Dino wants to e-a-t. Say it slow: eet. Eat!

He munches the leaf. Yum. His pals come to help.

Dino has a t-ea-m. Say it slow: teem. Team!

The team digs a deep pit. Dig, dig, dig!

In the pit is a bone. A real dino bone!

Dino wants to r-ea-d about it. Say it slow: reed. Read!

A kid book tells him facts. Nat Geo Kids has dino facts, games, and art. New facts come out all the time!

Dino grins. Slow is fine. Slow is smart.

Say it slow: leaf, eat, team, read.

You did it, just like Dino!

transcript.title: Oat and the Night Sky Dino
transcript.text:
Maya reads a new fact. "Some stars make shapes in the night sky!"

"Let's look, Oat," she says.

They wait for dark. They take a quilt to the green field by the oak tree.

The sky is deep blue. Then black. Stars peek out, one by one.

Maya sees three bright stars in a row. "That is a tail!" she says.

She traces more stars. A neck. A head. A row of teeth!

"Oat, it is a sky dino!"

Oat lifts his snout and gives a soft roar. The stars seem to gleam back.

A streak zooms past. A shooting star!

"Make a wish," Maya says.

She shuts her eyes tight. She wishes for more days like this one.

Oat leans close. Maya leans on his warm side.

Soon both of them sleep, under the sky dino.
transcript.cover_scene: A girl and a big green dinosaur lying on a quilt in a dark grassy field, gazing at stars that form a dinosaur shape.

chapters.title: Dino and the Great Track Trail
chapters.text:
Dino woke up on the grass. The sun was bright. Just then, he saw a track!

"A big track!" said Dino. "Let me read it. Tr-ack. Track!"

He took a step. Then a slow step. The trail went past a stump.

Gr-een grass. Gr-ay stone. St-ick. St-omp. Dino said each chunk slow, then fast.

"Sl-ow. Slow," said Dino. "I can say it!"

The trail went up a green hill. Dino ate a leaf on the way. He did not eat the whole tree!

At the top sat Stella. She had big feet and a long tail.

"You made this track!" said Dino.

"Just for fun," said Stella. "Now we are a team."

They sat in the grass and read a book of dino facts. Some dinos were as tall as trees! Some had teeth like sticks.

"Gr-eat book," said Dino. "Great!"

transcript.title: Oat and the Shell Shop
transcript.text:
Maya and Oat check the beach. They wish to find shells.

The shop by the dock sells dino things. A chart of dino facts hangs in the shop. Maya reads it. "New dino facts show up each year!"

"May we shop?" Maya asks.

The shop man grins. "Pick a thing that you wish for."

Maya picks a white shell. It has a shine like a tooth.

Oat shoves his snout in a dish of chips. Crunch! He chomps them all.

"Oat!" Maya says. "You must share!"

Oat shuts his mouth. He looks shy.

Then Oat digs in the sand with his chin. He finds a shell! It is thick and pink.

He puts it in Maya's hand.

"Thank you," Maya says. "This shell is the best."

They march home as the sun sinks.

chapters.title: Stella and the Stone Stump
chapters.text:
Stella the Stegosaurus stood by a stone stump at the edge of the stream. She had read that scientists still find new dinosaurs every year, and she wanted to find one too.

"St-ump," she said slowly. "Stump!" The stump was strong and old, and something was stuck under it.

Slim the Slothosaurus slid down the slope to help. "Sl-ow," he said. "Go slow, Stella."

Together they strained. Stomp, stomp! The stump moved. Under it lay a long, striped bone, still and cold.

"A strange bone!" said Slim. "Str-ong. Str-ipe. Str-ange!"

Stella stared. This bone did not match her team. It did not match Slim. It was a brand new dinosaur, sleeping under the stump for a million years.

They ran up the steep street of stones to tell the herd. Every dinosaur came to see.

"We found it," said Stella proudly. "Step by step, chunk by chunk, slow and strong."

chapters.title: Stego on Stone Street
chapters.text:
Stego was a strong stegosaurus with stiff plates down her spine. She lived near a steep slope at the end of Stone Street.

One still morning, Stego spotted a strange thing. A stack of straw sat on an old stump.

"St-ump," she said slowly. "Stump!"

She stepped closer and sniffed. Under the straw slept a small, striped baby dino. It slid out and blinked.

"Are you lost?" Stego asked.

The baby stood and stretched. It could not speak yet, so it just stamped its feet.

Stego let the baby stay close. They strolled down the street, past a stream and a strip of tall grass. Stego went slow so the baby could keep step.

At last, a big dino came stomping up the slope. The baby squealed and ran straight to her.

Scientists still study dinos like Stego. Brand new facts and art show us how strange and strong they were!

transcript.text:
Maya and Oat go to the fish tank hall.

Oat gives a soft huff.

The octopus waves one arm. Maya waves back.

chapters.title: Stripe the Shore Octopus
chapters.text:
Maya stood very still by the tide pool at the shore. Down in the cool water sat a small octopus with striped arms. Maya called him Stripe.

Stripe stretched one arm out slow, then slid it back. His arms were never stiff. He could squeeze through a slot no wider than a straw!

Maya said the tricky words the way she likes best: st-ood, stood. str-etched, stretched. sl-id, slid. Each chunk snapped together fast.

A sea turtle swam past the stones. Maya knew a fact about turtles: some turtles can stay under the water for hours while they sleep! Stripe stared at the turtle and turned a stony gray, just like the rock.

"You are a strong little star," Maya said.

Stripe stretched up one striped arm, almost like a wave goodbye. Then he slid under a stone and stayed still until the tide came back.

transcript.title: Five Sea Giants
transcript.text:
Maya sees a show. It tells about five huge beasts in the sea, long ago.

The first one has a long neck. It eats fish. It sails in the deep sea like a boat.

The next one has a wide tail. It beats the waves. It leaps and lands with a big splash.

The third one is a speedy one. It streaks past like a train. It reaches for a meal.

The fourth one has teeth like nails. Maya peeks from her seat. "Yikes!"

The last one is the biggest. It is as long as a road! Its jaw can eat a whole seal.

Maya reads the last screen. "These beasts lived in the sea. Each one was real!"

Oat leans on Maya.

"Do not be afraid," she says. "They swam here long ago."

chapters.title: Strong Streak the Sea Turtle
chapters.text:
Streak was a small sea turtle with one gold stripe on her shell. She wanted to swim to the far reef, but the waves were strong.

"Say it in chunks," said Mom. "str-ong. Strong. You are strong too."

Streak stretched her flippers. Str-etch. Stretch! She swam past a straw-thin eel and a string of shiny bubbles.

Near the rocks, a tiny fish was stuck in a strand of net. Streak did not stop. She pulled the strand straight until the little fish shot free.

"Thank you!" the fish said. "I hatched at a big aquarium in Chicago. People there raised a baby frogfish from an egg, the first time ever! Then they help us learn the sea."

Streak grinned. She swam down the reef street of coral, her gold stripe flashing.

Str-eak. Streak. A strong little turtle, strong all the way home.

transcript.text:
Maya watches a show with Dr. Scott. He digs up bones and shares what he finds.

"Long ago, big reptiles filled the oceans," he says. "They lived when dinosaurs did."

"This tooth is real," he says. "It chomped fish!"

Maya wishes she could dig with him.

She grabs a dish and a brush. She digs in the sand patch.

Crunch! She finds a shell.

"Such a good find!" she shouts.

chapters.title: Shelly the Shy Shark
chapters.text:
Shelly was a shy shark who lived in a shady reef. She liked to hide in the thick kelp and watch the fish flash by.

One day, a thin fish named Thad swam up. "Shelly, will you show me the shell cave?" he asked.

Shelly shook her head. "I am too shy," she said.

Thad said, "Think of it like this. Say it in chunks: sh-ell. Shell! Now swim with me."

So Shelly swam. She dashed past a starfish and a strong stream of bubbles. The shell cave was full of shiny pink shells.

Then a dolphin splashed in to say hello. "Did you know dolphins are born tail-first?" she said. "We shoot out backward!"

Shelly laughed. "That is the best fact I ever heard!"

"Thank you for showing me the cave," said Thad.

Shelly smiled with all her teeth. A shy shark can still make three fine friends.

transcript.title: Oat and the Sea Animal Team
transcript.text:
Oat wants a team. He roars, "Who will join me?"

A sea turtle floats by. "I will!" she says. She can glide for miles and hold her breath a long time.

A shark speeds up. "I will!" he says. He has rows of teeth and never needs sleep.

An octopus creeps from a crack. "I will!" she says. She has eight arms and three hearts!

A croc waits in the reeds. "I will!" he snaps. He can stay still for days.

Oat grins. "Now we are a real team."

They race down the coast. The turtle leads. The shark keeps pace. The octopus rides on Oat's back.

Maya waits on the beach with a pail of treats.

"Great job, team!" she calls.

Each one gets a snack. Oat gets seaweed. The team eats by the sea until the sun goes down.

chapters.title: Swift the Frilly Seahorse
chapters.text:
Swift was a small seahorse with a frilly fin. He wanted to swim fast, but his tail kept curling around the fresh green weeds.

"Try chunking it," said Frida the fish. "Say sw-im. Swim!"

"Sw-im. Swim!" said Swift. He swished his frill and swam three quick loops.

A dolphin swept past with a sweep of her tail. "Did you know dolphins are born tail-first?" she said. "My tail came out before my nose!"

Swift laughed. "My tail is the best part of me too."

They swam to a sweet, fresh stream of bubbles near the shore. Frida showed Swift how to float still while the water swirled.

"Fr-ends. Friends," Swift said slowly. "Friends! That word is easy now."

The three of them swam home as the sun sank. Swift swished his frilly fin and thought, a swift tail is good, but fresh friends are better.
